headline: Romania's top defence council accelerates Black Sea surveillance and mine/drone counter-capability after >=7 cargo ships hit near'
dek: Romanian defence council: accelerate development of maritime surveillance, naval-mine countering and anti-drone capabilities; threats to freedom of navigation and critical energy projects in the Black Sea pose a security crisis; strengthen deterrence/defence posture on the Eastern Flank — VERIFIED…
sources: Romanian Supreme Council of National Defence; NATO announcement (Tuesday); Reuters via Straits Times
fault_line: Is Russia running a deliberate 'boiling frog' test of NATO in allied waters — and should NATO move from surveillance to armed ship escorts?

sections.what_happened: Romanian defence council: accelerate development of maritime surveillance, naval-mine countering and anti-drone capabilities; threats to freedom of navigation and critical energy projects in the Black Sea pose a security crisis; strengthen deterrence/defence posture on the Eastern Flank — VERIFIED FACT of decision. >=7 cargo ships hit near Romanian/Bulgarian coasts in past two weeks, ~30 sailors dead or missing; Romanian F-16s shot down 2 Russian drones over Romanian waters Saturday — ATTRIBUTED REPORT via council/Reuters. NATO said Tuesday it will send more maritime patrol aircraft, radar systems and drones to the Black Sea — VERIFIED FACT of announcement.
sections.what_disputed: Attribution of the drone attacks to Russia rests on the Romanian council's framing ('direct consequences of Russia's aggression beyond Ukraine's borders'); per-incident authorship not independently itemized; no Russian response in reporting.
sections.why_matters: NATO's waters are on fire: 7 ships, 30 sailors, and the alliance finally moves metal into the Black Sea
sections.context: Background: NEW — Romania's top defence council accelerates Black Sea surveillance and mine/drone counter-capability after >=7 cargo ships hit near Romanian/Bulgarian coasts in two weeks (~30 sailors dead/missing); NATO sending more maritime patrol aircraft, radar and drones (Reuters/Straits Times, Oct 22)

totw_analysis: Our read: NATO's waters are on fire: 7 ships, 30 sailors, and the alliance finally moves metal into the Black Sea The fault line our audience is arguing over: Is Russia running a deliberate 'boiling frog' test of NATO in allied waters — and should NATO move from surveillance to armed ship escorts?
